comparison.interpretation: On this 2-case subset, OpenCode/big-pickle delivered no valid repair inside the bound on either case (0/2), while CodeForge's fixed free route at least converged to terminal, honestly-failed states on both (and passed 33/40 overall). The subset is too small for a general capability ranking; the defensible statement is that CodeForge's verification stack produces truthful terminal verdicts where a peer agent produced unbounded non-completion.
whereCodeForgeTrails: Plan completeness: 3 public failures share one signature - plan omitted selection/verification/uncertainty statements (AT-01, AT-02, PQ-01). Frontier agent CLIs generally emit richer explicit planning contracts.

Routing/authority-boundary fidelity under context pressure (CP-01, CP-02): report synthesis collapsed governance boundaries - a domain where larger frontier models with bigger context budgets perform better.

Tool-loop convergence on malformed-input reasoning (RP-02, 41 tools, ~3.1x mean): the free-route model did not converge on the malformed-vs-valid distinction; stronger models typically resolve such classification in fewer steps.

Capability ceiling is bounded by zero-cost routing: the fixed route is a small free model; paid-tier competitors (Codex, Claude Code) have materially larger models, and the Codex quota block itself shows hosted competitors also hit capacity walls.
